solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Restrain mongrel beginning to bite

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, taken here from bite

explanation.surface: A dog owner is told to hold back a mongrel that has started to bite.
explanation.definitionFit: To check or hold back something is to keep it under control, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Incompatible peacekeepers set to tour part of UK

parts.note: UN, the United Nations, sends peacekeeping forces

indicators.note: to tour is to go around, so the word for set surrounds the next piece

parts.note: to set, like jelly, is to congeal
NI is Northern Ireland, part of the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: Mismatched peacekeepers are about to travel around a region of Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people who cannot get along are disagreeable to each other, which is a mismatch of temperament.

clue.text: Bravo Ted and Linda, engaged after such a meeting?

parts.note: Bravo is B in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: engaged, like gears meshing together, says the letters of the two names are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Applause for Ted and Linda, who got engaged after meeting through a setup.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'engaged' reads as a betrothal, but it works as the signal to shuffle the two names; 'after' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A romantic meeting arranged between two strangers is the kind of encounter described, and the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: See controller teasing man on board

parts.note: arch means playfully mischievous or teasing, as in an arch smile
a bishop is one of the chessmen on a chessboard

explanation.surface: Someone flirtatiously mocks a fellow passenger, or perhaps a director, aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is not the verb but a noun: a see is a bishop's diocese, and the senior bishop over a province of sees is the one meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is a diocese, and the church dignitary presiding over the principal see of a province governs it.

clue.text: Eternal princess's elegance resurrected in part

indicators.note: resurrected says the hidden letters are read backwards
in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A princess's timeless grace is brought back to life, at least partly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that never grows old or dies is everlasting, the sense of eternal.

clue.text: Cook to study catering for small business

indicators.note: to cook figures or a story is to rework it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to a would-be chef to learn catering in order to run a small firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like a noun or a kitchen verb, but it signals the rearrangement of all of to study catering.
explanation.definitionFit: Small-scale manufacturing carried on in people's homes is a modest enterprise, a little firm.

clue.text: Bitter British beer not all drunk

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer

indicators.note: not all means the word for drunk loses a letter, its last

parts.note: full is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A British bitter, a kind of beer, not all of which has been drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bitter' poses as the British beer; here it means hostile.
explanation.definitionFit: A menacing or malevolent look is hostile and harmful, the sense of bitter as resentful.

clue.text: Crowd in garden on either side of road

indicators.note: on either side of means the word for garden is split around the next piece

parts.note: to garden is to hoe, working the soil

explanation.surface: A crowd gathers in a garden by a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A large unruly throng or mob is a multitude, the same as a crowd.

clue.text: Winger exercises intelligence

parts.note: PE, physical education, is exercises at school
wit is mental sharpness, intelligence

explanation.surface: A wide footballer works out to sharpen his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' suggests a footballer; here it is a bird, the lapwing.
explanation.definitionFit: The lapwing, a plover, is a bird, and so something with wings: a winger.

clue.text: Old volume, one to do with choppers belonging to the West

parts.note: cc, cubic centimetres, is a measure of volume
I is the Roman numeral for one
choppers is slang for teeth, and dental means relating to teeth

explanation.surface: An ancient book about helicopters, or teeth, comes from the Western world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Choppers' suggests helicopters or axes; here it is slang for teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Occident is the West, so something Western in origin is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Black line that has wrinkles

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a row is a line of things side by side

explanation.surface: A dark line that has creases in it, perhaps on old fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: the part of the face that creases when one frowns.
explanation.definitionFit: The forehead is the part of the face where lines and furrows appear with age or worry.

clue.text: Nervous, like one about to dive?

definitions.meaning: jittery and tense, as anxious people are
a diver stands right at the brink of the board or pool before jumping

explanation.surface: A tense swimmer stands poised, about to plunge in.
explanation.definitionFit: Being tense is to be at the brink emotionally, and a diver literally stands at the rim before plunging.

clue.text: Old king rejected excess cover with trees

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the king's name is read backwards

parts.note: Offa was an eighth-century king of Mercia, of Offa's Dyke fame
the rest is what is left over, the surplus

explanation.surface: An old monarch, spurned, decides to plant a forest over his surplus land.
explanation.walkthrough: Offa ruled the Anglo-Saxon kingdom of Mercia and built a long earthwork along the Welsh border.
explanation.definitionFit: To plant land with woodland is to turn it into forest, which is exactly this verb's meaning.

clue.text: Drug becoming old hat, doing the rounds for love

parts.note: speed is slang for amphetamine
dating means going out of date, becoming old-fashioned

explanation.surface: A drug becomes passé while it circulates among lovers.
explanation.walkthrough: At such events participants rotate round the tables, having a few minutes with each potential partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Singles move from table to table meeting partners briefly, literally circulating in search of romance.

clue.text: Dairy product female disposed of, recoiling

indicators.note: recoiling means springing back, so the word for disposed of is read backwards

parts.note: to dispose of food is to eat it, so ate

explanation.surface: A woman throws away some milk or cheese and recoils from it, perhaps because it has gone off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disposed of' suggests binning; here it means eaten up.
explanation.definitionFit: This crumbly white Greek cheese made from sheep's or goat's milk is one example of dairy food.

clue.text: Walk, run, climb on it

parts.note: a step is a pace, part of walking
a ladder is a run in tights or stockings

explanation.surface: A short instruction list: walk, run, then climb on it, like a fitness routine.
explanation.walkthrough: A ladder is the British word for a run in stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: A folding set of steps is something one mounts to reach high places, so the definition describes its use.

clue.text: Passed on antibody, one of forbidden seven

parts.note: to have passed on is to have died, so dead
a lysin is an antibody that destroys cells

explanation.surface: Someone died and passed on an antibody, one of seven banned things.
explanation.definitionFit: Christian tradition lists seven grave vices, such as pride and greed, each one forbidden.

clue.text: Amateur poet's written about one chap from Riga

indicators.note: written about means the poet's name is set around the other pieces

parts.note: Dante is the Italian poet; the 's reads as 'is'
I is the Roman numeral for one
a Lett is a Latvian, and Riga is the Latvian capital

explanation.surface: An Italian poet writes a piece about a Latvian man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chap from Riga' is a Latvian, called a Lett; 'poet's' supplies the Italian author of the Divine Comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A dabbler who takes up an art for pleasure rather than as a profession is a non-professional.

clue.text: Yankee to give away clothes for children's store

indicators.note: clothes is a verb here: to clothe is to dress, so the words cover the next piece

parts.note: to shop someone is British slang for betraying them to the police
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An American hands over clothes to a children's shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' looks like garments but is a verb, to cover; 'give away' is British slang for informing on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop selling playthings is a store aimed at children.

clue.text: Bar to discharge about 150

indicators.note: about means the word for discharge goes round the next piece

parts.note: to exude is to ooze or discharge
CL is 150 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A bar is about to discharge some 150 drinkers.
explanation.definitionFit: To shut someone out or ban them is to keep them out, the verb sense of bar.

clue.text: Sidekick's scheme's last to start

definitions.note: the 's reads as 'is': the clue says sidekick is, a helper or assistant

indicators.note: the final letter of the word for scheme is moved to the front

parts.note: an idea is a plan or scheme; the 's reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: A sidekick's plan has its final element brought to the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last to start' moves the final A of IDEA to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: An assistant, especially to a politician or officer, is a helper or right-hand person, a sidekick.

clue.text: Endearing expression unruly boys use around Lima

indicators.note: around says the scrambled letters go round the next piece
unruly means disorderly, so the letters of boys use are set in a new order

parts.note: Lima is L in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Rowdy lads use a fond phrase while in the Peruvian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unruly' makes BLESSYOU from BOYS USE, and 'around' places L inside after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the kindly phrase said when someone sneezes, also used to thank someone warmly.

clue.text: Supporter that is about to leave money

indicators.note: to leave means these letters depart from the word for supporter

parts.note: a brassiere is a supporting undergarment
IE, id est, means that is
RE means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A supporter, that is, is about to leave with the money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to leave' takes IE and RE out of BRASSIERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass is informal British slang for cash, from the coins once made of it.

clue.text: Stock web joke?

parts.note: E, as in e-mail and e-commerce, denotes things on the web
a quip is a witty joke

explanation.surface: Is an online gag a standard one, a stock joke?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' looks like an adjective, as in a stock joke; it is the verb meaning to supply.
explanation.definitionFit: To furnish or supply with what is needed is to provision, as one stocks a shelf.

clue.text: Pass left and right, initially making arrest

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass

indicators.note: initially means the first letter is taken from the word and

explanation.surface: A police officer passes left and right, beginning to make an arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: To nab or seize a suspect is informal police slang for apprehending them, the same sense as arrest.

clue.text: Border on piece of 21D, taking a turn

indicators.note: taking a turn means the instrument's name is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: 21 Down is brass, and a tuba is a piece of brass, an instrument in a brass section

explanation.surface: Part of something brass, turned round, lies alongside an edge.
explanation.definitionFit: To be adjacent to or share a boundary with something is to adjoin it, as neighbouring plots do.

clue.text: Chase Percy, dropping small diamonds, say

indicators.note: dropping means one letter is let fall from the nickname

parts.note: Harry Percy was nicknamed Hotspur, as in Shakespeare's Henry IV
diamonds is one suit in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A man named Percy loses some small gemstones.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Henry Percy, the medieval rebel, was known as Hotspur.
explanation.definitionFit: A close pursuit of a fleeing quarry is a chase, the phrase usually used of police following criminals.

clue.text: Fool European collecting new trophy for parasitic plant

indicators.note: collecting means taking in, so the fool and European go around the next piece

parts.note: a sap is a gullible fool

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the letters of trophy are rearranged

explanation.surface: A foolish European picks up a freshly won trophy for a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges the letters of trophy, and 'collecting' places them inside the fool and the European.
explanation.definitionFit: This organism lives off dead or decaying matter; the clue calls it a parasite loosely, as it feeds on other material.

clue.text: Sound of equine expending energy nearby

indicators.note: expending means using up, so the letter for energy is spent and removed

parts.note: a horse's cry is a neigh
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A horse whinnies, using up its energy, somewhere close by.
explanation.definitionFit: This old-fashioned word means near or close at hand, a synonym for close by.
